evidence: Cic. Phil. 5.19: homo vehemēns et violentus (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 34.32.3: tyrannus saevissimus et violentissimus in suōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of people, tempers and rule, and of wind, rivers and the sea (Lucr., Verg.). Violence itself is vīs (see force).

evidence: Cic. Vat. 4: vehemēns ferōxque nātūrā (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Eager and forceful rather than brutal; of an orator it can be praise (Cic. Brut. 88). Often written vēmēns (Ter., Catull., Lucr.).

phrases.latin: nāvigābāmus ā Cassiopā Brundisium mare Īonium violentum et vāstum et jactābundum
phrases.english: we were sailing from Cassiope to Brundisium over the Ionian sea, violent, vast and heaving
